AbstractText.Label: AIMS AND OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To: a. investigate pre and post-operative anxiety levels in parents of surgical patients; b. identify factors that affect parental anxiety; c. analyze assistance provided and overall parental satisfaction in order to assess if and how this aspect can impact their anxiety level.

AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Surgery as an event generates anxiety in children and their parents. Children who are anxious before surgery are likely to develop more postoperative psychological and physiological complications than those who are not. The role parents play in influencing emotional states of their children has been well demonstrated. However, specific national programs aimed at helping parents develop new models for coping are relatively inexistent in Italy.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: One hundred and one parents of children undergoing surgery at a healthcare facility in Padua, Italy completed the Italian version of the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory Form Y questionnaire. They also answered questions about their parents' socio-demographic situation, the amount and quality of pre-operative information received, assistance provided, and their overall satisfaction with this information.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The pre-operative level of anxiety in parents who were interviewed was higher than Italian normative data, especially in Pediatric Cardiac Surgery and Pediatric Urology departments. Mothers had a significantly higher level of anxiety than fathers. Communicating possible complications of surgical procedures increased anxiety, while providing information about pre- and post-surgery nutrition and pain management and providing local anesthetic on children decreased parental anxiety. Parents expressed a sufficiently high level of satisfaction although they defined the hospital environment as uncomfortable.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Aspects of care that can make hospitalization less traumatic for parents are: greater support, involving them in the treatment process, improving hospital department admission procedures and providing thorough pre-operative information.
